document.title: Session of the CC CPSU Politburo, January 17, 1980
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Politburo session with extensive discussion of the situation in Afghanistan after the invasion. Lyakhovsky and others report that top leaders secretly deliberated early withdrawal at the same time.

persons.name: Leonid I. Brezhnev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CC CPSU; chaired Politburo session

mentions.quote: we tasked a Commission made up of Comrades Andropov, Gromyko, Ustinov, and Ponomarev

persons.name: Iurii V. Andropov
persons.role: Politburo member; member of Afghanistan Commission; reported on Afghan party and state leadership

mentions.quote: In the last ten days in Afghanistan all the organs of party and state leadership were created

persons.name: Andrei A. Gromyko
persons.role: Soviet foreign minister; Afghanistan Commission member

mentions.quote: In the leadership of Afghanistan, a consolidation of forces is going on.
K. Babrak appealed to us for advice, whether he should go to the conference.

persons.name: Dmitrii F. Ustinov
persons.role: Soviet defense minister; Afghanistan Commission member

mentions.quote: USTINOV reports in detail the military situation in varius areas of Afghan territory

persons.name: Boris N. Ponomarev
persons.role: CC CPSU secretary; Afghanistan Commission member

mentions.quote: PONOMAREYV speaks about the type of measures which have been taken regarding the creation of the party

persons.name: Babrak Karmal
persons.role: Afghan leader (PDPA/NDPA, Parcham) heading the Afghan regime

mentions.quote: Babrak Karmal listens very attentively to the advice of our comrades.
Three very imposing tribes annnounced their support for the Babrak regime.

persons.name: L.I. Grekov
persons.role: Head of group of 16 Soviet advisers sent to Afghanistan

mentions.quote: a group of our advisers consisting of 16 people, with Com. Grekov, L.I. at the head of it,was sent to Afghanistan
Vance came out agains the participation of the USA in the Olympic Games.
Giscard d'Estaing sent a message. It is better.

organizations.name: CC CPSU Politburo
organizations.notes: Established a Commission (Andropov, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev) on Afghanistan, continued with same membership.

organizations.name: NDPA
organizations.notes: Ruling Afghan party; Parcham and Khalk factions still distinct.

organizations.name: NATO
organizations.notes: No unity on measures toward USSR.

organizations.name: UN General Assembly
organizations.notes: Voted resolution with 104 delegations in favor.

organizations.name: Afghan Army
organizations.notes: Said to support the Afghan leadership.

organizations.name: Afghan rebels
organizations.notes: Resistance hotbeds said to be fewer.

places.name: Islamabad
places.significance: Site of an Islamic conference; Babrak advised not to attend.

events.description: Politburo session on Afghanistan; Commission continued with same membership.
Group of 16 Soviet advisers headed by Grekov sent to Afghanistan ('yesterday').
Islamic conference meeting in Islamabad; Soviets advised Babrak not to go.
Politburo session on situation in Afghanistan; Commission retained with former membership.
UN General Assembly session ended with a resolution on Afghanistan passed by 104 delegations, 48 abstaining or opposing.
Islamic conference scheduled in Islamabad; Babrak advised not to attend.
Over ten days, all organs of party and state leadership created in Afghanistan, including a procurator.
Group of 16 Soviet advisers led by Grekov sent to Afghanistan.

sources_cited: Archive of the President of the Russian Federation, Fond 3, Opis 120, File 44
key_claims: The Politburo kept the same four-member Commission (Andropov, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev) to oversee Afghanistan policy.
Gromyko claimed the Afghan military situation had not worsened and that the army supports the leadership.
Andropov said Parcham–Khalk divisions persisted and tribes were key to winning support for the Babrak regime.
Ustinov described the military situation as basically satisfactory with fewer rebel hotbeds.
Soviets advised Babrak Karmal not to attend the Islamabad Islamic conference.
A 16-person Soviet adviser group led by Grekov was sent to Afghanistan to help build the party.
